comments.body:
RESOLVED for the immediate blockage, by the operator's chosen option: pin this gate environment.

CHANGE: Gerrit 1355, MERGED (`846b: pin the maintainer gate environment`), one file, +23 lines —
`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` gains env_id `ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5` with the
public half of this environment's op-cert key
(`ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIBJYVGrlY0lry1wXJUH16LysXt4NezYJ98El+EK1yuo3 rebar-opcert`).
LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submitted; `main` is 75cdfec3572 and the pin reads back from it.

ERA START IS NOT BACKDATED. `added_at_log_position` is `1785855397918577001-d97467a4-…`, the
tickets-branch tip at the moment of pinning — deliberately NOT reached back over the certs this
environment had already written. Those stay outside the era and had to be re-signed, which is
exactly story 4214's anti-backdating property and the reason the era model uses tickets-branch log
positions rather than main SHAs. Re-signing was free (`sign-review` replays the recorded
REVIEW_RESULT sidecar; no LLM re-run).

VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE GATE'S OWN CLASSIFIER, not by pushing and hoping:
    >>> classify_plan_review_attestation("129e-2d88-cce2-492c", repo_root=".")
    {'verdict': 'stale-head', 'reason': 'attestation is stale (unscoped; signed at 75cdfec357…)'}
    >>> bucket_for_verdict('stale-head')
    'accepted'
Before the pin this same call returned `mismatch` ("signing environment … is not pinned"), whose
bucket BLOCKS. After the pin the keyring lookup succeeds, so the classifier proceeds past the
keyring arm to the drift arm — and `stale-head` is one of the arms the gate explicitly ACCEPTS
("Code drift is ACCEPTED … punishing them would make the gate flaky-by-design"). That is the
mechanism, confirmed locally before any CI spend.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT GRANT, recorded because it is the security question this ticket turns on: the
pin makes this environment's plan-review certs VERIFIABLE. It does not widen who may VOTE.
`LLM-Review` and `Verified` are still cast only by the bots, so a change still cannot self-approve;
what changed is that a plan review this environment genuinely ran is no longer rejected purely on
provenance. The loader still refuses an unknown env (checked: a bogus env_id returns None).

STILL OPEN — this ticket is NOT fully discharged by the pin, and should stay open for the rest:
  * AC1/AC3 remain unmet in the general case. Pinning one maintainer environment unblocks THIS
    maintainer; it does not give an arbitrary contributor a path, and the failure message still
    does not name a remedy — an author who hits it must still reverse-engineer
    trusted_environments.yaml and the compose file to learn why a PASSING plan review was
    rejected. Both of those were the substance of AC2/AC3.
  * The deeper gap is unchanged: the op-cert service has no client in this repo and never persists
    what it signs, so "get a prod-attested plan review" is still not an executable instruction.
  * Worth deciding separately: whether the not-pinned arm should be ADVISORY when NO developer
    environment is pinnable, so the gate degrades to a warning instead of an unconditional block
    the first time anyone new hits it.

comments.body:
## RCA — mechanism proven (rebar-debug Phase 1)

**Root cause (single, changeable artifact):** `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`,
the not-pinned arm of `classify_plan_review_attestation` (the `keyring is None` branch, ~L238-246).
The classifier resolves the DSSE principal from the attestation envelope, calls
`trusted_env.trusted_env_keyring(principal, repo_root)`, and returns an affirmative
`{"verdict": "mismatch"}` whenever that principal is absent from `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`.
`mismatch` is in `FLAG_VERDICTS`, so `bucket_for_verdict` returns `flag` and
`apply_bugfix_size_gate` sets `verdict["verdict"] = "BLOCK"`. The rejection is on the SOURCE of
certification (who signed), never on whether a plan review actually happened.

**Discriminating runtime proof:** `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py::test_classify_unpinned_foreign_environment_flags`
executes the classifier against a real fixture store holding a genuinely minted, genuinely signed,
same-material plan-review op-cert whose env is simply not pinned. It observes `verdict == "mismatch"`
and `bucket == "flag"`. Its sibling `test_classify_pinned_foreign_environment_reaches_accepted`
holds every other variable constant and differs ONLY in whether `trusted_environments.yaml` pins
the env — and reaches `certified`/`accepted`. The pair discriminates provenance from plan quality:
identical review, identical material, opposite verdicts. Both pass on `main` today, so the arm is
live, not theoretical.

**Legitimacy:** `defect` / `incomplete-implementation` against this ticket's own AC1 and AC3 (the
authoritative statement of intended behaviour), which the 75cdfec357 pin left unmet.

## Fix plan (operator's design decision — implemented as current policy, not a config framework)

The attestation check must NOT gate on the SOURCE of certification. It gates ONLY on the FACT that
an attested plan review has been completed, plus that attestation's lifecycle/freshness validity.

1. `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` — delete the cross-host source-of-certification
   chain: the `trusted_env_keyring` lookup + not-pinned `mismatch` arm, the `verify_opcert` call,
   and `_plan_review_anchor` (whose only consumer was `verify_opcert`'s era anchoring). The chain
   becomes: attestation record present -> decodable op-cert envelope -> `compute_validity`
   lifecycle/freshness. The verdict vocabulary shrinks to the `compute_validity` literals plus the
   gate's own `error`; unknown literals still fail OPEN (infra/advisory).
2. `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py` — RED oracle: invert
   `test_classify_unpinned_foreign_environment_flags` into
   `test_classify_unpinned_foreign_environment_is_accepted`, and realign the vocabulary tests.
3. `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — new section documenting the Gerrit bugfix-size attestation gate
   and its executable remedy (AC1).
4. `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — the author-facing on-ramp for the same (AC1).
5. AC3 is satisfied by removal: the message that named no remedy is gone, and the only remaining
   blocking finding is the teaching finding, which names `rebar review-plan <id>`.

Explicitly out of scope, and deliberately so: no op-cert service client, no configurable
trust-policy framework. This is the current policy, "for now".

comments.body:
## rebar-debug final report — Phase 2 complete, change on Gerrit

**Gerrit change 1404** (`846b: gate on the fact of a review, not its source`), patchset 2 at
`18699e3ace`. Plan review: **PASS, signed**, `certified` (`verified_at_sha 18f08d57c0`).

**Proven root cause.** `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`, the `keyring is None` arm of
`classify_plan_review_attestation`. An unpinned DSSE principal returned an affirmative
`{"verdict": "mismatch"}`, which is in `FLAG_VERDICTS`, so `apply_bugfix_size_gate` set
`verdict["verdict"] = "BLOCK"`. Rejection was on the SOURCE of certification, never on whether a
plan review happened.

**Proof.** The paired fixture experiments hold everything constant except pinning: same minted,
signed, same-material op-cert reaches `certified`/accepted when the env is pinned and `mismatch`/flag
when it is not. Replication on the REAL reported case: with `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`
DELETED — the exact reported condition — `classify_plan_review_attestation('129e-2d88-cce2-492c')`
now returns `stale-head` -> `accepted`. Pre-fix, the identical call returned
`mismatch` ("signing environment 'ade0f2ef-…' is not pinned") -> `flag` -> BLOCK. That is Gerrit
1344's sole blocking finding, gone, and gone WITHOUT depending on the 1355 pin.

**RED->GREEN.** Oracles `test_classify_unpinned_signing_environment_is_accepted` and
`test_oversized_bug_fix_reviewed_in_an_unpinned_environment_does_not_block`, both observed FAILING
first (`mismatch` / `BLOCK`) and HELD OUT from the implementing subagent (moved out of its tree,
path declared off-limits). Mutation check: re-inserting the exact root cause returns both to RED;
restoring the fix returns them to GREEN. They assert observable return values, not private names,
so they are not change-detectors.

**The fix.** The chain is now four steps: record present -> decodable op-cert envelope -> SUBJECT
BINDING (ticket id + kind, read from the SIGNED payload) -> `compute_validity`. The
`trusted_env_keyring` lookup, the `verify_opcert` call, and `_plan_review_anchor` are gone. The
verdict vocabulary shrank to the `compute_validity` literals plus `error`; unknown literals still
fail OPEN, so the removal can never become a surprise block.

**The plan review earned two real improvements** (it BLOCKED twice before passing, correctly):
1. It caught that deleting `verify_opcert` would silently drop SUBJECT BINDING as well, since that
   was its only home — `opcert_from_record` merely decodes and `compute_validity` checks no ticket
   id. Binding is now re-asserted explicitly in this module, with two regressions
   (`test_classify_rejects_a_cert_bound_to_another_ticket`,
   `test_classify_rejects_a_cert_of_another_kind`, the latter proving a lying plaintext mirror
   loses to the signed payload). Without this, a valid cert replayed off another ticket would have
   been accepted.
2. It forced AC2's security reasoning to be written down rather than asserted, and AC4 to be
   restated to match the adopted policy instead of contradicting it. Both are now in the
   description and mirrored in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

**Scope & safety.** Caller sweep: `finalize.py` (signature unchanged) and `review_bot/retrigger.py`
(behaviour changes BY DESIGN — the same unsatisfiability seen from the recheck-review side — and
stays fail-closed on every non-accepted bucket, 15 tests pass). No new dependency; the fix restores
a path rather than creating capability; no pre-existing test was weakened — the two vocabulary
tests changed expectations literal-for-literal because the vocabulary itself shrank by design, and
gained a new assertion that the removed literals cannot linger in the BLOCKING bucket.

**Siblings.** Construct sweep for `trusted_env_keyring(...) is None -> affirmative reject`: two
sites total. The one fixed here, and `trusted_env.verify_required_environment`, whose only consumer
is `rebar verify-opcert` — a close-AUDIT surface gated on an explicitly CONFIGURED required
environment with its own enforcement window and grandfathering. Not a sibling: there the
environment is chosen deliberately by config, not imposed on every contributor. Parity census
(CLI / MCP / library / automated callers / dual direction): `review-code` N/A (Gerrit-only by
design), no MCP surface, library + both automated callers go through the shared core and inherit
the fix. The dual-direction slot is the finding worth recording — the claim gate and the close gate
NEVER consulted `trusted_env` (confirmed: no reference outside `attest/trusted_env.py`,
`verify_opcert.py`, `trusted_env_cmd.py`). The code-review gate was the lone outlier, so this
change moves it INTO line with rebar's other attestation consumers rather than out of it.

**Residual risk.** Accepted, with reasoning recorded under "Security reasoning" in the description
and in the docs: this criterion is now an anti-sloppiness gate, not an anti-adversary one, because
the attestation record lives on the attacker-writable tickets branch and there is no trust root for
an unpinned signer. The adversarial boundary remains `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`, both
bot-only, on a Gerrit-gated code branch. Nothing here widens who may vote.

**AC status.** AC1 met (documented in `docs/plan-review-gate.md` + the packaged
`rebar explain review` guide; demonstrated end to end on real change 1344/129e, not by inspection).
AC2 met (reasoning recorded, alternatives weighed, reversibility stated). AC3 met (the message that
named no remedy is deleted; the teaching finding names `review-plan` / `sign-review` /
`review-plan --status`). AC4 restated and met under the operator's decision.

NOT CLOSING until 1404 is `Verified +1` and merged.

compiled_state.description:
# The bugfix-size attestation gate is unsatisfiable for any locally-reviewed bug

## Context / Problem

`bugfix_size_gate.py` (landed on main 2026-08-03, commit 1920dc9fe5) BLOCKS a Gerrit change whose
`rebar-ticket:` bug carries >150 non-test changed lines unless that bug has an acceptable
plan-review attestation. Its "cross-host verification" design constraint is explicit:

    the review bot is NOT the environment that signed the attestation, so this module verifies
    the op-cert against the PINNED `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` keyring (never the bot's
    own env key), mirroring `verify_required_environment`'s not-pinned arm for unpinned
    principals.

`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` pinned exactly ONE environment when this ticket was filed:
`9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65` (`nava-opcert-prod`), whose private half "lives ONLY in
SSM /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key".

> **Correction, as of the reviewed tree.** That file now pins **TWO** environments: Gerrit 1355
> (merged, `75cdfec357`) added `ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5`, this maintainer's own gate
> environment, and that is the principal which signed `129e`'s attestation. The paragraphs below
> describe the pre-1355 state and are kept as the ticket's history. The pin resolved the blockage
> for ONE machine and is precisely why this ticket stayed open: it did not make the criterion
> satisfiable for anyone else, and pinning is CODEOWNERS-gated so a contributor cannot self-serve
> it.

A plan review run by a developer signs with that developer's own env id as the DSSE principal. That
principal is not pinned, so `trusted_env_keyring(principal, repo_root)` returns None and the gate
takes its not-pinned arm:

    {"verdict": "mismatch",
     "reason": "signing environment '<env>' is not pinned in trusted_environments.yaml"}

which is an affirmative invalid classification, so it BLOCKS (it is not one of the fail-open
infrastructure arms, and it is not one of the ACCEPTED `stale-code`/`stale-head` drift arms).

**So a large bug fix can only clear this gate with an attestation produced by the prod op-cert
environment — and there is no way to obtain one.** The deployed `opcert` service does accept
`{"ticket_id", "kind": "plan-review"}` on `POST /opcert/jobs` and signs with the SSM key, but:

1. **no client exists in the repo.** `grep` for `opcert/jobs` outside `opcert_service/app.py`
   finds only the nginx template, the terraform output description, and unit tests. Callers are
   expected to SigV4-sign to an API Gateway endpoint; nothing in `rebar` does.
2. **the service deliberately cannot persist what it signs.** compose sets
   `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "off"` with the comment "a gate's SIGNATURE append lands only in the
   discarded per-job workspace". It returns the `envelope` in the job record, and there is no
   rebar CLI that records a returned envelope onto a ticket as its attestation.
3. **the guard is a production secret.** `/opcert/jobs` fails closed without the
   `X-Opcert-Guard` header, materialized from SSM `/rebar/prod/opcert-origin-guard`.

## Evidence this is live, not theoretical

Gerrit change 1344 (bug `129e-2d88-cce2-492c`, 554 non-test lines) is **`Verified +1`** with its
only blocking finding being this criterion. Its plan review PASSED and was re-signed locally;
the gate's complaint moved from "unsigned; no plan-review attestation record" (patchset 1) to
"mismatch; signing environment 'ade0f2ef-…' is not pinned" (patchset 2), i.e. the signature IS
seen and is rejected solely on provenance. No code finding blocks the change.

`129e` in turn `blocks` epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76`, so this gate currently blocks an epic.

## Why no existing bug fix hit this first

The gate landed 2026-08-03. The only recent bug fix over the floor, `e3cd-ba36-41c3-4661`
(229 non-test lines), merged 2026-08-02 — ONE DAY BEFORE the gate existed — and carries no
attestation at all (`review-plan --status` -> "unsigned"). So there is no precedent path; 129e
appears to be the first change to actually meet this gate.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` — the not-pinned arm's severity/classification.
- `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` — whether developer signing environments are pinnable at all.
- a missing client for the op-cert service (submit + record the returned envelope), if the
  intended answer is that large bug fixes must be prod-attested.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` / the packaged code-review guide — neither tells an author how to
  obtain an acceptable attestation for a large fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a large bug fix authored in a developer environment has a DOCUMENTED, EXECUTABLE path to an
      attestation this gate accepts — demonstrated end to end on a real change, not by inspection
- [ ] the not-pinned arm's behaviour is a deliberate, recorded decision: either it stays blocking
      and the path above exists, or it is reclassified (e.g. advisory when NO developer environment
      is pinnable), with the security reasoning written down
- [ ] the failure message names the remedy, so an author hitting it is not left to reverse-engineer
      trusted_environments.yaml and the compose file to discover why a PASSING plan review is
      rejected
- [ ] the gate still requires a genuine, PASSED, signed plan-review attestation BOUND TO THIS
      ticket and kind, so an unreviewed change cannot self-certify. RESTATED under the operator's
      design decision (see "Security reasoning" below): trust now rests on the FACT of a completed
      attested review, NOT on the signing environment's provenance. The original wording
      ("does NOT let a change self-certify from an untrusted environment") described the
      provenance-gated design that this ticket exists to retire, and is superseded.

## Fix plan (operator's design decision — implemented as current policy, not a config framework)

The attestation check must NOT gate on the SOURCE of certification. It gates ONLY on the FACT that
an attested plan review has been completed, plus that attestation's lifecycle/freshness validity.

1. `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` — delete the cross-host source-of-certification
   chain: the `trusted_env_keyring` lookup + not-pinned `mismatch` arm, the `verify_opcert` call,
   and `_plan_review_anchor` (whose only consumer was `verify_opcert`'s era anchoring). The verdict
   vocabulary shrinks to the `compute_validity` literals plus the gate's own `error`; unknown
   literals still fail OPEN (infra/advisory).

   **`verify_opcert` also carried the subject binding (its Phase 0), so deleting it would drop
   that too — therefore the binding is RE-ASSERTED IN THIS MODULE, explicitly, as its own step.**
   `verify_opcert` was the only site enforcing it; nothing downstream replaces it
   (`opcert_from_record` merely decodes, and `compute_validity` verifies no signature and checks no
   ticket id). The new chain is four steps, not three:

   1. attestation record present, else `unsigned`;
   2. decodable op-cert envelope, else `unsigned`;
   3. **subject binding, read from the SIGNED payload's predicate** (`bound["ticket_id"]` and
      `bound["kind"]`, never the record's plaintext mirror): a cert minted for a different ticket,
      or of a different kind, returns `wrong-kind` -> FLAG -> BLOCK. This is kept because it asks
      WHAT the attestation covers, not WHO signed it, so it is orthogonal to the provenance
      question this ticket retires — and it is what stops a valid cert being replayed off another
      ticket;
   4. `compute_validity` lifecycle/freshness (`stale-material`, `stale-reopened`, phase, pins).

   What is NOT retained, stated without euphemism: step 3 reads the signed payload but nothing
   re-checks the DSSE signature, because with no pinned key there is no trust root to check it
   against. See "Security reasoning" for why that is the deliberate choice and what it costs.
2. `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py` — RED oracle: invert
   `test_classify_unpinned_foreign_environment_flags` into
   `test_classify_unpinned_foreign_environment_is_accepted`, and realign the vocabulary tests.
3. `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — new section documenting the Gerrit bugfix-size attestation gate
   and its executable remedy (AC1).
4. `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — the author-facing on-ramp for the same (AC1).
5. AC3 is satisfied by removal: the message that named no remedy is gone, and the only remaining
   blocking finding is the teaching finding, which names `rebar review-plan <id>`.

Explicitly out of scope, and deliberately so: no op-cert service client, no configurable
trust-policy framework. This is the current policy, "for now".

## Testing

RED-first. The proving oracle is `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py::test_classify_unpinned_signing_environment_is_accepted`
plus `::test_oversized_bug_fix_reviewed_in_an_unpinned_environment_does_not_block`, both of which
mint a genuinely signed plan-review op-cert from an unpinned principal in a fixture store with no
`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` at all. Both were observed FAILING on `main` with
`verdict == 'mismatch'` / `'BLOCK'` before the fix existed, and were held out from the implementer.

- `pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py -q` — 37 passed (was 35 + 2 red).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py -q` — 15 passed; the
  `recheck-review` re-check stays fail-closed on every non-accepted bucket.
- Mutation check: re-inserting the exact root cause (the `trusted_env_keyring(...) is None ->
  mismatch` arm) returns both oracles to RED; restoring the fix returns them to GREEN.
- `pytest tests/unit -q` — 4313 passed, 9 skipped.
- Subject-binding regressions (added on plan-review feedback):
  `test_classify_rejects_a_cert_bound_to_another_ticket` and
  `test_classify_rejects_a_cert_of_another_kind` — both must classify `wrong-kind` (BLOCK).
- Replication on the REAL reported change, not a fixture (AC1): with
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` DELETED — the exact condition in the report, no developer
  environment pinnable at all — `classify_plan_review_attestation('129e-2d88-cce2-492c')` returns
  `stale-head` -> bucket `accepted`. Before the fix the identical call returned
  `mismatch` ("signing environment 'ade0f2ef-…' is not pinned") -> bucket `flag` -> BLOCK.
  That is Gerrit 1344's blocking finding, gone, without the pin.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — both clean (mypy: 432 files, no issues).


## Security reasoning (AC2 — the deliberate, recorded decision)

**What was removed and why there is no middle path.** The old chain verified the DSSE signature
via `verify_opcert` against the keyring `trusted_env_keyring(principal)` returns — i.e. against
`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`. That file IS the trust root. When the principal is not pinned
there is NO key to verify against, so "keep signature verification but relax only the not-pinned
arm" is not actually a posture: an attacker simply signs with an unpinned principal and takes the
relaxed arm. The two coherent options are (a) every accepted attestation must be signed by a pinned
key — which is unsatisfiable for any contributor, since pinning is CODEOWNERS-gated on the code
branch and no contributor can add themselves; and (b) accept the FACT of a recorded, well-formed,
subject-bound, lifecycle-valid plan-review attestation. The operator chose (b), for now.

**What that costs, stated plainly.** The attestation record lives on the auto-pushed, non-Gerrit-
gated tickets branch, which `opcert.opcert_from_record` documents as attacker-writable. Under (b)
this criterion is therefore an ANTI-SLOPPINESS gate ("did you actually write and review a plan
before shipping 150+ non-test lines under a bug label?"), not an ANTI-ADVERSARY one. Anyone able
to write the tickets branch can fabricate a record that satisfies it.

**Why that is acceptable here.** This gate was never the adversarial boundary. Landing on `main`
still requires `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`, both cast only by bots/admins, plus no unresolved
comments — so a fabricated attestation buys an attacker nothing except the removal of one coaching
block. The code branch itself remains Gerrit-gated and CODEOWNERS-protected, which is where the
pin file and the review rubric live. Nothing in this change widens who may vote.

**What is retained.** Subject binding is kept — re-implemented as an explicit step in
`classify_plan_review_attestation` because `verify_opcert` was its only previous home (see Fix plan
step 1.3) — because it asks WHAT the attestation covers rather than WHO signed it: a cert bound to another ticket, or of another kind,
classifies `wrong-kind` and BLOCKS (regressions
`test_classify_rejects_a_cert_bound_to_another_ticket`, `test_classify_rejects_a_cert_of_another_kind`,
the latter proving the lying plaintext mirror is ignored in favour of the signed payload).
Lifecycle and freshness are untouched: `stale-material` still blocks, so attest-then-edit-the-plan
is still not a bypass. A missing attestation is still `unsigned` -> BLOCK, which is the gate's
whole point. Unknown verdicts still fail OPEN, so the removal can never become a surprise block.

**Why not the pinning alternative (Gerrit 1355, already merged).** Pinning env `ade0f2ef-…` fixed
the blockage for ONE maintainer's machine while leaving the criterion unsatisfiable for everyone
else — it is the reason this ticket stayed open after that change landed. Scaling it means pinning
every contributor's environment in a CODEOWNERS-gated file, i.e. an admin round-trip before anyone
can land a large bug fix, and a growing keyring whose entries are never revoked. That trades a
real, recurring delivery block for a security property this gate does not actually provide (see
"What that costs"). The pin stays in place and still verifies where it applies; it is simply no
longer load-bearing for this criterion.

**Reversibility.** "For now" is not a promise of a mechanism. Restoring provenance gating is
re-adding the keyring lookup + `verify_opcert` call to `classify_plan_review_attestation`; the
`ACCEPTED`/`FLAG`/`INFRA` partition and the fail-open default are unchanged, so nothing else has to
move. No config key, flag, or policy framework is introduced — deliberately, since a switch nobody
can flip safely is worse than an explicit, documented policy.

## Affected consumers (beyond the edited files)

`src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py` is not edited but its behaviour changes by design: it reuses
this module's `classify_plan_review_attestation` + `bucket_for_verdict` for the self-service
`recheck-review` precondition, so an attestation from an unpinned developer environment now
unlocks a re-review where it previously refused. That is the intended outcome (it is the same
unsatisfiability bug seen from the retrigger side) and it stays FAIL-CLOSED: any bucket other than
`accepted` still refuses. Covered by `tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py`
(15 passed).

RED oracle: an unpinned signing environment must now reach accepted; realign the verdict vocabulary tests
document the Gerrit bugfix-size attestation gate and its executable remedy (AC1)
author-facing on-ramp for the same executable path (AC1)

compiled_state.title: bugfix-size attestation gate is unsatisfiable for any locally-reviewed bug — only the prod op-cert env is pinned and it has no client
